'''Virginia Joanne Torczon''' is an American [[applied mathematics|applied mathematician]] and [[computer scientist]] known for her research on [[nonlinear optimization]] methods including [[Pattern search (optimization)|pattern search]]. She is dean of graduate studies and research, and chancellor professor of computer science, at the [[College of William & Mary]].{{r|wm}}

==Education and career==
Torczon majored in history as an undergraduate at [[Wesleyan University]].{{r|parprof}} She earned her Ph.D. in mathematical sciences in 1989 from [[Rice University]].{{r|parprof|mg}} Her dissertation, ''Multi-Directional Search: a Direct Search Algorithm for Parallel Machines'', was supervised by [[John E. Dennis]].{{r|mg}}

Before becoming dean of graduate studies and research at William & Mary, she was the first female chair of the computer science department there.{{r|wydaily}}

==Recognition==
Torczon's paper "On the Convergence of Pattern Search Algorithms" won the inaugural [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM) Outstanding Paper Prize for the best paper published in a SIAM journal in 1999.{{r|outstanding}}
